Xi, Putin Meet Ahead of Historic Trump Trilateral Summit — Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin meet in Shenzhen ahead of a historic summit with Donald Trump, with Ukraine, Iran, nuclear disarmament and global trade expected to feature in discussions. The talks have raised concerns that the three leaders could reshape global power relations and make decisions affecting Ukraine without Kyiv or Europe.

Ukraine Says It Took Down Crimean Bridge Arch Without Musk’s Starlink — Ukraine brought down a major section of the Crimean Bridge using drones and missiles without Starlink or Starshield, relying on a homegrown communications system. The strike exposed Russian air defense weaknesses and dealt a symbolic blow to Putin ahead of his summit with Trump and Xi.

Xi, Trump, Putin: What Can the Trilateral Summit Achieve? — The proposed trilateral summit between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen highlights China’s growing diplomatic influence but raises concerns over its geopolitical ambitions. European media question Beijing’s claims of neutrality, warn of limited progress on Ukraine and nuclear disarmament, and criticise Trump for lending legitimacy to authoritarian leaders while sidelining Europe.

Russian Drone Strikes on Dnipro Injure Six, Including 15-Year-Old Boy — Russian drone attacks on Dnipro and the surrounding region injured six people, including a teenager, with one woman hospitalized in serious condition.

Ukraine to Triple Deep Strikes as Allies Pledge New Weapons at Ramstein — Ukraine announced plans to more than triple its deep-strike capabilities in 2027, despite US criticism of attacks inside Russia. Germany and Britain defended Kyiv’s strategy as Western allies pledged hundreds of millions in new military assistance.

Ukraine Charges Russian Vice Admiral Over Kyiv Strike That Killed 13 — Ukraine has charged Russian Vice Admiral Arkady Romanov in absentia with war crimes over a July 2024 missile attack on a Kyiv residential building that killed 13 civilians, including five children. Investigators say he organized the strike on orders from Black Sea Fleet commander Admiral Sergei Pinchuk.

Rutte Says Continued Military Aid to Ukraine Is Essential to Securing Peace — NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte warned that Russia could intensify its attacks on Ukraine this winter, urging allies to maintain military support for Kyiv as essential to securing peace and strengthening its position at the negotiating table.

UK Hands US Army Officer Suspected of Spying for Russia Over to American Custody — British authorities have transferred a US Army officer suspected of spying for Russia to American military custody following an espionage investigation involving US and UK intelligence agencies.

Germany Calls US Criticism of Ukraine’s Deep Strikes ‘Stupid’ — German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius and British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting rejected US criticism of Ukraine’s long-range strikes inside Russia, exposing disagreements among NATO allies over how Kyiv should fight the war.

UN: Ukraine’s October Civilian Casualties Up 95% From October 2025 — Civilian casualties in Ukraine were 95% higher in October than in the same month last year, the United Nations Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine (HRMMU) said in a report published on Tuesday, Nov. 17. According to the report, at least 372 civilians were killed and 1,981 injured – the highest toll for any October since Russia’s full-scale invasion began in February 2022. Missile and drone attacks caused more than half o

Putin Arrives in Shenzhen Ahead of First Trilateral Summit With Trump, Xi — Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Shenzhen, China, on Tuesday, Nov. 17, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, where he will hold the first-ever trilateral meeting with US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday, Nov. 19. According to the Kremlin, the agenda has been agreed upon and a separate Putin-Trump meeting is being prepared, although Ukraine’s place in the di

No Survivors Left as Russian An-12 Military Plane Crashes in Siberia — A Russian An-12 military transport plane crashed near the village of Yagunovo in Siberia’s Kemerovo region on Tuesday, Nov. 17, killing all 19 people on board, according to the Russian news outlet Baza. The aircraft was reportedly carrying spare parts from Novosibirsk to Kansk when its crew reported an emergency and tried to land in Kemerovo. Experts believe leaked fuel most likely ignited in one of the plane’s four engines,

Zelensky Offers Allies Missile Exchange, Seeks 40 More F-16s at Ramstein — President Volodymyr Zelensky offered its Western allies on Tuesday, Nov. 17 to hand over air defense interceptors from their current stocks in exchange for newer missiles Kyiv has already ordered. Addressing the Ukraine Defense Contact Group (UDCG) by video, he also requested 40 more F-16 fighter jets, European Mirage jets and long-range weapons to counter Russia’s ballistic missiles, many of which Moscow receives from No

Kyiv Partially Reopens South, North Bridges After Russian Strike — Kyiv has partially reopened both the South and North bridges across the Dnipro River after Russia’s overnight attack, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said on Tuesday, Nov. 17. The South Bridge is open to one-way traffic from the Left Bank to the Right Bank for vehicles weighing up to 10 tonnes and public transport up to 18 tonnes. The North Bridge is open only to public and special transport, while private cars and transit freight vehicle

US Loses Measles-Free Status as Cases, Deaths Mount — The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) announced on Tuesday, Nov. 17, that the United States has lost its measles elimination status, 26 years after it was first declared measles-free in 2000. The country is facing its largest outbreak in more than three decades, with over 5,400 cases recorded this year, nearly all among unvaccinated people. Health experts have blamed falling vaccination rates and distrust fanned by President Donald Trum

Russia’s Geran Drone Spotted Over Moldova’s Capital — A Russian drone was spotted over Moldovan capital Chisinau on Tuesday, prompting authorities to restrict the country’s airspace over security concerns. The incident came as a Geran-2 drone, identified by Moldova’s Defense Ministry, entered the country’s airspace twice from Ukraine’s southern Odesa region. Videos shared by local media showed the aircraft over several areas of the capital.

UK to Supply Ukraine With 1,000 Air Defense Missiles Starting December — UK Defense Secretary Wes Streeting announced on Tuesday, Nov. 17, that the UK will supply Ukraine with more than 1,000 short-range air defense missiles and launchers, along with more than a dozen radars, under a £240 million ($317 million) winter package. He made the announcement while co-chairing the Ukraine Defense Contact Group at NATO headquarters in Brussels. Deliveries are expected to begin as early as mid-December.

Ukraine Pitches 10 More Humanitarian Operations in Russian-Occupied Territories — Ukraine has proposed 10 additional humanitarian operations in Russian-occupied parts of the Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions following an operation in Oleshky. Zelensky said the proposals would be discussed with US mediators as Kyiv prepares for expanded peace talks in Berlin.

Ukraine Prepares Major Prisoner Swap After US-Led Talks — Ukraine is preparing a prisoner exchange with Russia following US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi, Zelensky said. Kyiv is ready to secure releases in the coming weeks, though the timing depends on Moscow and US mediators. Negotiators are discussing a swap that could return more than 1,000 people to each side – potentially the war’s largest – as well as the release of Ukrainian civilians, including some held since before Russia’s full-scale in

NATO’s Rutte Defends Ukraine’s Strike on Crimean Bridge — NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said Ukraine’s defense against Russia includes striking logistical hubs, responding to the attack on the Crimean Bridge on Nov. 17. He said media footage suggested the operation had succeeded but cautioned that the precise circumstances and extent of the damage still needed to be established.

Ukraine’s Allies Pledge €70M for Demining — The Netherlands, Norway, the European Union and Finland have pledged €70 million ($77 million ) to support humanitarian demining in Ukraine, Prime Minister Serhii Koretskiy said on Tuesday. The commitment was made during the Ukraine Mine Action Conference (UMAC 2026) in Brussels.

Kyiv Moves 3 Districts to Backup Heating After Attack — Kyiv is switching some consumers in the Darnytskyi, Obolonskyi, and Podilskyi districts to backup heating after Russian strikes damaged heating mains at the North and South bridges on Tuesday. Affected consumers will temporarily lose hot water while Kyivteploenergo inspects and repairs the damaged networks.

US Recce Plane Did Crimea Close Fly-by Hours Before Ukraine Hit Critical Bridge — US and NATO intel, surveillance, and recce (ISR) aircraft patrolled near Crimea hours before Ukraine successfully targeted the Kerch Bridge. Russian Z-bloggers allege NATO helped identify Russian air defenses and coordinate the attack. Bulgaria also deployed aircraft and ships after the sinking of Betul 8.

Russia Hits US-Owned Bunge Plant in Dnipro for Third Time as Strikes on Ukrainian Businesses Mount — Since Saturday, Russian strikes have hit a Bunge-owned sunflower oil plant in Dnipro – the third attack on it this year – along with a Kyiv restaurant chain’s warehouse, the Ekipazh window factory and the Korolivskyi Smak food plant. The attacks point to a shift in Russian targeting toward Ukraine’s food industry, which accounts for 60% of the country’s exports.

Trump Open to Separate Putin Meeting in China — Donald Trump on Tuesday said that he would be willing to meet Vladimir Putin separately during his China visit, without confirming a bilateral appointment. Both leaders are scheduled to join Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on Thursday. Moscow says it is working on separate talks, including discussions of Russia’s war against Ukraine.

Hungary Suspends Ukraine Rail Links After Russian Drone Strike — Hungary has suspended rail connections with Ukraine for two days following a Russian drone attack in the Zakarpattia region. The drone struck about 300 meters (984 feet) from the Mukachevo train station, prompting the evacuation of a Hungarian train crew and temporarily restricting cross-border services.

‘Putin’s Favorite Toy’: Russian War Bloggers Fume After Crimean Bridge Arch Collapses — A Ukrainian strike on Nov. 17 sent a 227-meter arch of the Crimean Bridge crashing into the Kerch Strait, setting off recriminations among Russia’s biggest pro-war bloggers – some mocking Moscow’s air defenses and the bridge’s construction, others demanding escalation. President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine used a mix of Ukrainian-made drones and missiles – the Palianytsia, Neptune, Ruta and Flamingo – in

Cargo Ship Sinks Off Bulgaria After Attack by 2 Naval Drones — The cargo ship BETUL 8 sank in the Black Sea off Bulgaria on Monday, Nov. 16, after an attack by two naval drones, according to the Bulgarian maritime outlet. All 12 crew members were rescued in an operation involving Bulgarian, Romanian and Turkish vessels and aircraft. The incident adds to a series of earlier attacks on commercial shipping near Bulgaria and Romania.

Germany to Allocate $300M for Ukraine’s Patriot Missiles — Germany has pledged $300 million to buy US weaponry for Ukraine through NATO’s Prioritized Ukraine Requirements List (PURL), German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius said on Tuesday. The money will prioritize PAC-2 and PAC-3 interceptors for Ukraine’s US-made Patriot systems, which guard against Russian ballistic missiles. Berlin is also helping integrate IRIS-T missiles into Ukraine’s NASAMS systems and supplying radars, F-16 ammunition

7 Ballistic Missiles Hit Kyiv’s Main Dnipro Crossings — Zelensky said seven Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv’s Southern and Northern bridges overnight, prompting repair and emergency transport plans. He also reported major power outages in three regions and outlined measures to protect infrastructure, maintain medical services, and support exports.

Japan Scrambles Fighters as Taiwan Tracks 2 Russian Planes — Japan said two suspected Russian aircraft violated its territorial airspace on Nov. 17, prompting scramble of fighter aircraft and a diplomatic protest to Moscow. Taiwan separately reported Russian military aircraft entering its air defense identification zone off its eastern coast. Sources say the accounts of the two countries may be based on the same aircraft, although that has not been confirmed.

Ukraine Needs Up to 2 Years to Build Own Ballistic Missile Defenses, Sweden Says — Ukraine will need 18-24 months to develop its own defenses against ballistic missiles, Swedish Defense Minister Pål Jonson said on Tuesday in Brussels, as Russia ramps up production. He called the Prioritized Ukraine Requirements List (PURL) – allied-funded purchases of US weapons – the most vital tool for Kyiv, noting Sweden has contributed $552 million. Separately, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine hopes

Kremlin Says Crimean Bridge Will Be ‘Better Than Before’ — Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov promised to rebuild and improve the damaged Crimean Bridge. Russia’s transport ministry said road and rail traffic had been suspended following another attack overnight on Monday and Tuesday, with specialists assessing the damage. The crossing connects Russia to occupied Crimea and serves as a supply route for Russian forces.

Russia Rejects Black Sea Ceasefire Without Full Peace Deal, Turkey Says — Russia is unwilling to agree to a temporary ceasefire in the Black Sea without a comprehensive peace deal with Ukraine, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said. He identified the dispute over Donbas – which Russia wants Ukraine to surrender – as the main obstacle to ending the war. The remarks come as Washington pushes competing proposals to halt the fighting.

Ukraine Must Work With the US From Both Sides of the Aisle — Despite the Democrats’ midterm victory and imminent control of Congress, Kyiv should continue to work with Republicans. Ukraine must make the West aware of how pivotal they now are to military innovation and how Russia only respects force.

‘We Couldn’t Fight Without It’: Ukrainian Commander Defends Mobilization — Brig. Gen. Sviatoslav Zaiets described mobilization as a heavy burden but said Ukraine’s military could not carry out its missions without it. Speaking at a forum attended by more than 250 NCOs, but stressed the need for better training and adaptation before combat deployment.
CARTOON: Preparations for the Big Meet of the 3 Accomplices — Serhii Kolyada’s ironic take on the latest international events.

US, Russia, Israel Likely to Oppose Convention Limiting Autonomous Weapons — The UN Secretary General called for nations to extend limitations on the use of autonomous weapons systems on Monday. Major arms producers such as the US, Russia and Israel look set to oppose the move.

From Flamingo to Neptune: Zelensky Reveals Details of Crimea Bridge Strike — Zelensky confirmed that Ukraine struck both the road and railway sections of the Kerch Bridge. He said the attack was the culmination of a seven-stage operation coordinated by the SBU and military leadership over several weeks.

2 Killed in Kyiv as Russian Attack Hits Residential District — A Russian attack on Kyiv’s Obolonskyi district killed two people and injured another, damaging residential and non-residential buildings. Rescuers pulled one person from the rubble, while a separate attack sparked a fire at a non-residential building in the Dniprovskyi district.

Ukraine Hits Major Russian Petrochemical Hub in Massive Drone Attack — Ukrainian drones targeted Russia’s Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat petrochemical complex in Bashkortostan, reportedly sparking a major fire, as attacks were also reported on the Crimean Bridge and an electrical substation in Kursk. Moscow claimed its air defenses intercepted 1,441 Ukrainian drones overnight, including around 800 reportedly heading toward the capital.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 16, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on November 16, 2026.

Crimean Bridge Arch Collapses Into Sea After Fresh Ukrainian Missile Strike — Zelensky and the SBU confirmed a Ukrainian strike that destroyed a major arch and road section of the Crimean Bridge in a month-long, seven-stage operation. The attack followed earlier drone strikes and came as Russia intensified attacks on Kyiv’s bridges.

Trump Pivots on Ukraine as Moscow Blocks Europe — President Donald Trump says he will discuss Ukraine with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping at Thursday’s summit in China, reversing earlier White House guidance. Meanwhile, European leaders are preparing a parallel summit in Berlin focused on Ukraine’s security guarantees and defense funding, as Moscow continues resisting Europe’s participation in peace negotiations.

IMF Reports Major Progress in Ukraine Talks, Bringing $1.6 Billion in Aid Closer — The IMF reported significant progress in talks with Ukraine on the second and third reviews of its $8.1 billion loan program. Successful completion could unlock $1.6 billion, although further agreements and board approval are required.

Russian Aircraft Violate Japanese Airspace, Triggering Fighter Jet Scramble — Japan scrambled fighter jets after two suspected Russian aircraft violated its airspace Tuesday, Nov. 17, prompting a diplomatic protest. South Korea also deployed fighter jets after Russian military aircraft entered its air defense identification zone.

Woman Pulled Alive From Rubble After Russian Strike on Zaporizhzhia — Ukrainian rescuers freed a 51-year-old woman trapped beneath rubble after a Russian strike on an industrial facility in Zaporizhzhia. Separate Russian drone attacks killed a driver and injured another woman.

N. Korea Sends Russia Dozens of Missiles Monthly: Zelensky — President Zelensky says Russia receives dozens of North Korean ballistic missiles monthly and is expanding domestic missile production. Meanwhile, the Kremlin says Putin could meet Kim Jong Un at this week’s APEC summit in China.

Russian Missiles Hit 2 Major Kyiv Bridges, Damage Critical Infrastructure — Russian missiles struck Kyiv’s North and South bridges late Monday, Nov. 16, damaging critical infrastructure and disrupting essential services. Three people were injured in the Cherkasy region as Russia launched attacks across Ukraine.

California Governor Newsom Visits Ukraine — California Governor Gavin Newsom announced new medical aid for Ukraine during a visit to Lviv on Sunday, Nov. 15, which includes a 50-bed field medical station, more than 1,300 hospital beds, over 11 million bandages and 20 generators. Newsom, who is reportedly weighing a 2028 presidential bid, visited Lychakiv Cemetery, a rehabilitation center, and defense tech companies. The visit comes less than two weeks after Democrats won both chambers of Congres

72 Dead in Russian Strike as Komyshuvakha Search Ends — Search and rescue operations concluded in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region on Monday, Nov. 16, two weeks after Russian forces launched guided-bombs on a humanitarian aid site. According to Ukraine’s National Police, the death toll climbed to 72, with four people remaining missing. Russia shelled the village 11 times during the search, injuring police officers and rescuers. ASELSAN Neutralizes 51 Drones Simultaneously — Turkish defense company ASELSAN said its EJDERHA AD 200 (Dragon) High Power Electromagnetic (HPEM) counter-drone system neutralized 51 airborne drones within seconds after their simultaneous launch. The company’s president claimed it was a world record.

Europe Joins Ukraine-US Talks in Full for First Time Ahead of Berlin Meeting — Europe’s E5 format – comprising Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Poland, along with EU institutions and NATO – joined talks with Ukrainian and US negotiators in full for the first time on Nov. 16, President Volodymyr Zelensky said. The discussion followed Nov. 10-11 Abu Dhabi negotiations with Russia and the US, from which the European side was excluded, as well as a meeting in Moscow between US envoys and Russian

Denmark’s Frederiksen Defends Rwanda Deportation Hub Despite Criticism — Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen on Monday, Nov. 16, defended a plan by Denmark, Austria, the Netherlands, Greece and Germany to set up a deportation center in Rwanda for rejected asylum seekers. French President Emmanuel Macron had criticized the idea of sending migrants to centers outside the EU. Speaking in Vienna, Frederiksen called the project “very modern” and said the current system is “broken.” The center wou

Trump Claims Putin Is ‘Backing Down,’ Would Like to See War End — Speaking to reporters on Monday, Nov. 16, US President Donald Trump said Russian President Vladimir Putin is “backing down” in the war against Ukraine, arguing that the Kremlin could be “a lot more tougher.” Asked about Starlink restrictions, Trump claimed he had not heard about them, despite repeated warnings from Kyiv that a speed cap on the service’s military version, Starshield, is preventing its drone operations. EU Sends Ukraine €1.71 Billion for Drones, Air Defense — Ukraine received €1.71 billion ($1.88 billion) from the European Union on Nov. 16 to buy drones, ammunition and air defense systems. Prime Minister Serhiy Koretskyi confirmed that the funds had reached the Treasury account. The payment comes under the EU’s existing Ukraine Support Loan, worth €90 billion ($99 billion), while Kyiv seeks predictable financing for 2027.

Moldova’s Sandu Backs Ukraine’s EU Bid as Von der Leyen Hails ‘Real Prospect’ of Enlargement — Moldovan President Maia Sandu backed Ukraine’s accession bid on Monday, Nov. 16, saying that she would welcome the day both Chișinău and Kyiv become EU members. Her remarks came as the European Commission prepares to close 25 negotiating chapters with Moldova and only seven with Ukraine, due to delays in Kyiv’s judicial and law enforcement reforms. Speaking at the opening of an enlargement forum in Bru

Kellogg: Xi Could Pressure Putin as Russia Leans on China — The former US envoy says Chinese leader Xi Jinping could pressure Putin toward a settlement because Russia is the junior partner in their relationship. Kellogg also backs European participation in negotiations and sees the Oleshky mission as a possible ceasefire model.

More Offensive, Fire Over the Baltic, Ballistics and Ball Bearings — Russian assaults in Donetsk region are suffering record losses as Ukrainian drone units hunt infantry far behind the lines. Ukraine hit Ust-Luga, Russia’s main Baltic oil port, in a complex strike that coincided with the loss of up to three Russian aircraft near St. Petersburg. Starlink problems returned, US-brokered talks went nowhere, NATO failed to down a single stray drone, and a senior Russian air force officer died in a S

Russia’s Oil Revenue Hits Record Since December 2022 — A think tank’s new report suggests that Russia’s oil revenue reached €754 million ($830 million) per day in October – the highest since December 2022, with seaborne crude exports accounting for most of the revenue. Despite the US-Russia diesel deal, the think tank estimated that Russian ports remain strained by Ukrainian strikes, with diesel loadings rising three-fold from September while overall seaborne export volumes dropped 8%.

Zelensky: Over Half of Russian Refinery Capacity Shut Down by Ukrainian Drones — Ukraine’s drone campaign has hit 27 of Russia’s 32 refineries. Zelensky says more than 55% of refining capacity is disabled; Bloomberg estimates nearly 40% offline. Recent attacks hit Azov fuel storage and Ilsky refinery, and shut Volgograd’s plant.

Canada Shuts the Door on Russian Hockey Players — The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) has confirmed that Russia's U20 team will not play at the 2027 World Junior Championship in Canada. Ottawa announced on Nov. 11 that Russian athletes will be denied entry even with valid visas. The ban comes weeks after the Court of Arbitration for Sport ordered Russia's return to international tournaments.

Russian Il-76 Likely Hit in Ukrainian Strike – Report — A Russian Il-76 military transport aircraft was likely hit during Ukraine’s Nov. 10 strike on Staraya Russa airfield, according to aviation monitoring channel AviVector. A satellite image published on Nov. 16 shows apparent damage around an aircraft at the site. Ukraine confirmed attacking the adjoining repair plant, but the extent of damage to the Il-76 remains unclear.

11M Russians ‘Don’t Have a Toilet’, Says Sikorski — Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski accused Russia’s leadership of caring more about territorial conquest than citizens’ living conditions, citing 11 million Russians without a toilet at home. His Sunday post followed reports that Moscow had revived demands to restrict NATO deployments and halt Western military aid to Ukraine. Poland and other European governments have rejected Russian attempts to dictate their security arrangements.

Russia Seeks Seats in UN Telecom Agency — Russia is seeking positions on two influential bodies within the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), a move diplomats say could help Moscow weaken its international isolation over its war against Ukraine. The elections are taking place at the agency’s conference in Doha, where member states are choosing representatives to lead its strategy, budget and radio regulations. Ukraine Highlights Media’s Role in Wartime Communication — Ukraine’s officials highlighted the contribution of radio, television and communications workers to the country’s wartime resilience, praising their role in countering Russian disinformation, documenting the consequences of Russia’s invasion and maintaining connections between people. The head of Ukraine’s emergency services said communications specialists continue working even under Russian attacks, helping connect those in need with em

EU Approves Record $8.8 Billion Payment to Ukraine for Reforms — The Council of the EU approved just under €8 billion ($8.8 billion) for Ukraine under the Ukraine Facility – the largest single disbursement yet under the program. Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said he expects the tranche soon, taking Ukraine’s 2026 total under the facility to €13.6 billion ($14.9 billion). The payment, the ninth under the Ukraine Plan, follows Kyiv’s completion of more than 20 reform steps.

Russia Prepares New Strike on Ukraine’s Grid, Air Force Warns — Russia is preparing another attack on Ukraine’s energy facilities and critical infrastructure, Air Force spokesperson Yuriy Ihnat said. Ukraine has received information about the preparations for several days and is awaiting additional air defense ammunition from partners. The warning follows repeated strikes that have damaged power infrastructure, prolonged outages and intensified pressure on repair crews ahead of winter, as Kyiv p

Ukraine Strikes Cut Russian Gasoline Supplies by 31% — Ukraine’s Defense Ministry said drone strikes on Russian oil infrastructure have disrupted nine major refineries, contributing to an around 31% drop in crude processing and worsening fuel shortages across several regions. President Zelensky said more than 55% of Russia’s refining capacity had been knocked offline. Monday’s latest attacks targeted an oil depot and a gas distribution station in Rostov Region.

Kremlin Gets Ready to Sell Russians a ‘Victory’ in Ukraine — The Kremlin has urged ruling-party deputies to prepare for a potential victory and the return of combatants from Ukraine. Earlier reports said Moscow was developing propaganda narratives to portray a possible peace deal as a victory despite heavy losses and limited gains.

Cybersecurity Experts Report 40% Increase in Cyberattacks on Russia in 2026 — The annual domestic cybersecurity threat study by the Moscow-based Positive Technologies independent cybersecurity thinktank published its annual threat study on Monday. It said that successful, reported attacks on Russian organizations rose by 40% year-on-year, from 433 to 605.

Moscow Conscripts Offered Drone Warfare Contracts Instead of Mandatory Service — Moscow is offering conscripts one-year contracts in Russia’s Unmanned Systems Forces instead of mandatory military service, as the Kremlin struggles to meet recruitment targets. Despite promises of lucrative pay and service away from the front, previous recruits have been sent to assault units in Ukraine.

EU Plans €45 Billion Ukraine Loan as 4 States Object — The European Commission plans to propose a new €45 billion loan for Ukraine, backed by the EU budget, the Financial Times reported. It would help cover Kyiv’s estimated €70 billion financing gap in 2027. Czechia, Slovakia, Hungary and Bulgaria oppose further contributions, complicating a proposal that would require agreement from all 27 member states.

600 Ukrainian Drones Targeted Moscow, Shot Down Overnight — Moscow’s mayor claimed that around 600 drones were shot down overnight with most intercepted at long distance from the capital. Russia’s Ministry of Defense said that a total of 1,336 Ukrainian drones were shot down in one of Kyiv's largest aerial attacks of the war.

The Kremlin Is Doubling Down on Its Maximalist Negotiating Strategy — Moscow is digging in with its “non-starter” demands while offering the White House apparent concessions aimed at improving the optics of cooperation with Russia. The strategy hopes to buy time until Western support for Ukraine falters.

Trump, Putin and Xi to Meet Without Set Agenda, Ukraine War Off Table — Trump, Putin, and Xi are expected to meet in China on Thursday without an agreed agenda, with nuclear arms control likely to dominate discussions and Russia’s war against Ukraine largely excluded. The meeting follows disagreements over its format and purpose, with Putin reportedly seeking a new Yalta-style arrangement, while Beijing resists direct involvement in Ukraine peace negotiations.

Russian Strikes Across Ukraine Kill 2, Injure at Least 12 — Russian attacks killed two people and injured at least 12 across Ukraine on Monday, Nov. 16, according to regional authorities. Strikes hit Dnipro and Zaporizhzhia, while Russian drones damaged energy facilities in Cherkasy region and critical infrastructure in the Vinnytsia region and Odesa.

Estonia Prepares to Run Government From Abroad if Russia Invades — Estonia is developing a digital contingency plan to run government services from abroad if Russia invades or occupies its territory. The strategy will use secure cloud systems and overseas data backups to keep essential state functions operating during a crisis.

Prince Harry Makes Surprise Lviv Visit to Back Veterans — Prince Harry made an unannounced weekend visit to Lviv, meeting wounded Ukrainian veterans and attending trials for the 2027 Invictus Games. He also addressed a Superhumans conference on treating war injuries, praised Ukrainian medical teams and expressed confidence in Ukraine’s victory. It was his fourth visit to the country since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022.

Ukraine - NATO Membership for Donbas? — Trump’s reported offer of NATO membership or similar security guarantees in exchange for Ukraine’s withdrawal from Donbas raises serious questions about US commitment and Russia’s intentions. Without firm US backing, such guarantees may be worthless.

NATO Drops Plans for 2027 Leaders’ Summit in Albania Amid Alliance Tensions — NATO is abandoning plans for a 2027 summit in Albania and reducing ministerial meetings amid disagreements over defense spending and broader tensions within the alliance. Albania could host a summit in 2028, while NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte says future gatherings will be organized when necessary.

Estonia to Close All Border Crossings With Russia After GRU-Linked Sabotage Attempt — Estonia will close all border crossings with Russia from Dec. 1 after thwarting an attempted explosion and arson attack on drone manufacturer Threod Systems. Authorities say the GRU recruited the suspects, eight of whom were detained in Latvia. The incident has prompted Moscow to accuse Tallinn of Russophobia and renewed warnings from Estonian officials about Russia’s broader sabotage campaign against European

Crimean Bridge Shut After Ukrainian Strike as Russia Claims Record 1,336 Drones Downed — Ukrainian forces attacked the Crimean Bridge overnight on Nov. 15-16, forcing its closure and delaying four trains traveling to occupied Crimea.
